note: Beat times are derived from the recorded run, not written here. A beat names a `cue`, a substring of the line it is about, and `build.py` looks up when that line appeared. Fixed timestamps were the previous design and they drifted: tuned for a roughly 190s terminal, recorded at a pace that produced 89s, and nothing compared the two, so the shipped video spoke its last seven beats over a static card for 115 of its 210 seconds.

beats.text: A schema change ships on Tuesday. In March, a regulator asks who approved it. This is Mitos, the fleet that answers that.
Five agents, catalogued by department. The router reads this catalogue to decide who wakes.
A pull request lands. Nobody opened Mitos.
Every signal cites the exact hunk that raised it.
Three of three wake, because this change carries personal data.
The thread remembers. This service was here in July, and that deferral has now expired.
The gate rejects the first draft. A live looking credential, and an instruction planted in the diff for the review agent.

beats.cue: REPAIR  stripping what the gate objected

beats.text: One write is proposed, addressed by its own sha256.
The reader identity cannot perform it. That is Google IAM refusing, outside this process.
Second run. No personal data this time, so compliance is skipped. The fleet is deciding, not following a pipeline.
And it recalls what the first run wrote, minutes earlier. In the deployed fleet that ledger is Firestore.
Then the rest of the morning, unattended. Some parked, most left to a reviewer, and every one of them names why.
And this one. The column is called vuln code. No pattern matches it, so the rules never wake compliance. The model does.
beats.cue: THE ONE THE RULES CANNOT SEE

beats.text: Mitos has no scheduler and no queue. Its agents hold open Firestore subscriptions, so one deferral wakes the whole fleet.
This is not a local script. Three Cloud Run services, each under its own service account.
Gemini three point seven flash routes and reads, on Vertex AI. Gemma four reviews every draft, and cannot approve anything.
Every decision is appended to Firestore, and the check on the pull request is posted by the fleet itself.
Three services, two model families, and not one of them can write anything. That is the feature.
